\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جمع} \fa{کردن} (jam' kardan)}{جمع کردن (jam' kardan)}]{\fa{جمع} \fa{کردن} (jam' kardan) — to tidy up; to gather}

\label{lesson:FA-C536-jam-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a homemaker, then the Persian for a capable housewife.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جمع} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{جمع} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{jam' kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to tidy up; to gather\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{اتاقشان} \fa{را} \fa{جمع} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchehâ otâqashân râ jam' kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children tidied their room.
\end{quote}

\emph{jam'} 'gathering' + \emph{kardan}. Also 'to collect' and, in sums, 'to add'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jam'} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{jamʿ}, 'gathering' (EtymDB). \emph{kardan}, 'to do', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jam' kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jam' kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{jam' kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a homemaker, then the Persian for a capable housewife, then say \emph{jam' kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خشک} \fa{کردن} (khoshk kardan)}{خشک کردن (khoshk kardan)}]{\fa{خشک} \fa{کردن} (khoshk kardan) — to dry}

\label{lesson:FA-C536-khoshk-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a capable housewife, then the Persian for to tidy up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خشک} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{خشک} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{khoshk kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to dry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{موهایش} \fa{را} \fa{با} \fa{حوله} \fa{خشک} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u muhâyash râ bâ hule khoshk kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She dried her hair with a towel.
\end{quote}

\emph{khoshk} 'dry' + \emph{kardan}. \emph{khoshk shodan} — to dry out.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khoshk kardan} is built on two inherited words: \emph{khoshk}, 'dry', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{hušk}, and \emph{kardan}, 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شلوغ} \fa{کردن} (sholugh kardan)}{شلوغ کردن (sholugh kardan)}]{\fa{شلوغ} \fa{کردن} (sholugh kardan) — to make a mess; to make a racket}

\label{lesson:FA-C536-sholugh-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to tidy up, then the Persian for to dry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شلوغ} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{شلوغ} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{sholugh kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to make a mess; to make a racket\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{خانه} \fa{را} \fa{شلوغ} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchehâ khâne râ sholugh kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children made a mess of the house.
\end{quote}

\emph{sholugh} 'crowded, busy, messy' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sholugh} was borrowed from Azerbaijani, a Turkic language (EtymDB). \emph{kardan}, 'to do', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نامرتب} (nâmorattab)}{نامرتب (nâmorattab)}]{\fa{نامرتب} (nâmorattab) — untidy, messy}

\label{lesson:FA-C536-namorattab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to dry, then the Persian for to make a mess.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نامرتب}}
\textbf{\fa{نامرتب}} (\emph{nâmorattab}) — \textquotedblleft{}untidy, messy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اتاق} \fa{برادرم} \fa{همیشه} \fa{نامرتب} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{otâq-e barâdaram hamishe nâmorattab ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother's room is always untidy.
\end{quote}

\emph{nâ-} 'not' + \emph{morattab} 'tidy', as in \emph{morattab kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nâmorattab} is built in Persian from the prefix \emph{nâ-}, 'not', and \emph{morattab}, 'in order', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{murattab}, 'arranged'. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آشغال} (âshghâl)}{آشغال (âshghâl)}]{\fa{آشغال} (âshghâl) — rubbish, trash}

\label{lesson:FA-C536-ashghal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to make a mess, then the Persian for untidy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آشغال}}
\textbf{\fa{آشغال}} (\emph{âshghâl}) — \textquotedblleft{}rubbish, trash\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{شبها} \fa{آشغالها} \fa{را} \fa{بیرون} \fa{میبرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedaram shabhâ âshghâlhâ râ birun mibarad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father takes the rubbish out at night.
\end{quote}

Everyday; \emph{zobâle} is more formal.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âshghâl} is the everyday word for rubbish, but EtymDB has no entry for it, and its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to make a mess, then the Persian for untidy, then say \emph{âshghâl} again
